entities.name: Peter, King of Hungary
entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Peter, known as Peter Orseolo or Peter the Venetian, was King of Hungary twice. He first succeeded his uncle, King Stephen I, in 1038. His favoritism towards his foreign courtiers caused an uprising which ended with his 1041 deposition. Peter was restored in 1044 by Henry III, Holy Roman Emperor. He accepted the Emperor's suzerainty during his second reign, which ended in 1046 after a pagan uprising. Hungarian chronicles are unanimous that Peter was executed by order of his successor, Andrew I, but the chronicler Cosmas of Prague's reference to his alleged marriage around 1055 suggests that he may also have survived his second deposition.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Peter's reign was marked by his favoritism towards foreign courtiers and his eventual deposition in 1041. He accepted suzerainty from Henry III during his second reign, which ended in 1046 after a pagan uprising.
